title: Omi /v1/screen HTTP Protocol
description: Hand-written schema-of-record for the screen-recording HTTP wire. DRAFT-v1 — pending David's ratification; sibling native-capture and Rewind lanes treat these shapes as their spec. Modeled on the listen schema's documentation conventions (x-omi-* annotations, closed additionalProperties, $defs as the single home for each payload). Pixels and H.265 chunks NEVER appear on this wire or in the service store: the client OCRs on-device and syncs text+metadata only.

x-omi-protocol.ratification: pending David; authorized as a NEW contract family by the 2026-08-15 screen-backend lane brief (DAVID-OVERNIGHT-2026-08-15-RULINGS.md full-parity with the legacy desktop Rewind sink)

privacy.rule: Frame pixels and 60s H.265 chunks stay on the capturing device. The service stores metadata, OCR text, block geometry, dhash, and an opaque client-local frame_ref so the native lane can garbage-collect chunks after retention.

auth.detail: uid derived server-side from the Authorization bearer token. Every path is owner-scoped (ownerAccountId). Missing or invalid credentials are 401 unauthorized.

paths.detail: Batched HTTP ingest. A WebSocket is not required for v1. One capture_session_id binds the batch; each frame carries its own captured_at, app identity, frame_ref, dhash, and OCR attachment. Duplicate identical ids are no-ops; a colliding id with different bytes is 409.
One local calendar day, ordered by captured_at ascending, with app identity on every row. Day is YYYY-MM-DD in the account timezone.
Which local days hold at least one surviving frame, plus oldest/newest captured_at and the live frame count.

Keyword (FTS) search over normalized OCR text. Hits carry a snippet and the block ids that matched, which power on-image highlight parity. Semantic/vector search is a seam: when unconfigured it returns status not_configured and does not affect FTS ranking.
Current retention window. Unset accounts report the default of 7.

days must be 3, 7, 14, 30, or 0 (unlimited, the legacy sentinel). Negative or unparseable values fail SAFE to unlimited (0) and never to a deleting window. A successful write sweeps that owner immediately.
frame_refs the service retired so the native lane can delete the corresponding local chunks. The service never held pixels.

invariants.title: Pixels never cross the wire
invariants.detail: Request and response objects forbid pixel, image, and chunk-byte fields. additionalProperties is false on every payload. A client-local frame_ref is the only handle to bytes that stay on device.

invariants.title: OCR blocks are required for highlight parity
invariants.detail: Every ingested frame carries full_text plus at least one block with text and normalized x,y,w,h,confidence. Search hits name the matched block ids so Rewind can highlight on the local image.

invariants.title: Retention 0 is unlimited; invalid never deletes
invariants.detail: The legacy sentinel 0 means unlimited. Negative, non-finite, or otherwise unparseable days coerce to 0. The default when unset is 7. A coerced-unlimited setting must not delete any row.

invariants.title: Owner scope is total
invariants.detail: Every read and write is keyed by the authenticated ownerAccountId. Another account's frames are indistinguishable from absence.

invariants.title: FTS is real; vector search is a seam
invariants.detail: Text search always runs FTS over normalized OCR. The embedding/vector source is optional configuration; the default adapter answers not_configured and must not invent ranking.

path.description: Client-local path of the 60s H.265 chunk that contains this frame. Never fetched by the service.

offset.description: Client-defined offset into that chunk (milliseconds into the 60s window at baseline). The service stores the integer opaquely.

ref.description: Opaque client-local handle. The service round-trips it; it must not be a URL the service would fetch.

FrameRef.description: Client-local locator for pixels that never leave the device. Tagged union: chunk path+offset, or an opaque ref.

id.description: Stable id within the frame. The client may supply one; the service defaults to the 0-based index as a decimal string. Search hits refer to this id.

x.description: Normalized left edge of the block in the captured frame, origin top-left.

y.description: Normalized top edge of the block in the captured frame, origin top-left.

w.description: Normalized width. x+w must not exceed 1 beyond a 1e-4 float slop.

h.description: Normalized height. y+h must not exceed 1 beyond a 1e-4 float slop.

confidence.description: On-device OCR confidence for this block (Apple Vision at baseline).

full_text.description: Concatenated OCR for the frame. Indexed by FTS5 after normalization.

blocks.description: Per-block geometry. Required: on-image highlight parity cannot be reconstructed from full_text alone.

id.description: Client-chosen idempotency key for this frame under the owner.

captured_at.description: UTC instant the focused window was captured.

dhash.description: Perceptual difference hash computed on-device. Not a pixel payload.

capture_session_id.description: Client identity for one capture session. Many frames share it.

inserted.description: false when this id was already stored with identical bytes (idempotent replay).

TimelineFrame.description: Timeline rows carry app identity and the client-local ref. OCR is omitted so a day page stays lean; search is the text surface.

day.description: Local calendar day in the account timezone.

days.description: Ascending unique local days that currently hold at least one frame.

snippet.description: OCR excerpt with matched terms wrapped in << >> (FTS5 snippet convention).

matched_block_ids.description: OcrBlock.id values whose text matched the query. Powers on-image highlight.

rank.description: Higher is better. FTS ranking (bm25 inverted to this polarity) for the keyword hits.

oneOf.description: Default. No embedding engine is wired; keyword hits are the whole result.
Reserved for a later embedding adapter. Not emitted by the draft-v1 default source.

days.description: 3, 7, 14, or 30 days, or 0 for unlimited (legacy sentinel). Default when unset: 7. Invalid input is coerced to 0, never to a deleting window.
